directAnswer: Pope St. Gregory II, a Roman, reigned from 715 to 731. He sent St. Boniface to evangelize Germany, encouraged the refounding of Monte Cassino, resisted the iconoclast policies and taxes of Emperor Leo III, and received from the Lombard king Liutprand the town of Sutri, often seen as the first step toward the Papal States.

sections.h2: Librarian, Deacon, and Companion to Constantinople
paras: Gregory was born in Rome, the son of Marcellus, and was raised in the papal household from a young age. Under Sergius I he became a subdeacon, treasurer, and later librarian of the Roman Church. As a deacon he accompanied Pope Constantine to Constantinople in 710–711, where his learning impressed Justinian II during the discussions about the Quinisext canons. He was elected pope in 715.

Early in his reign he began repairing the walls of Rome, a work interrupted by a severe flood of the Tiber. He also restored churches and founded or renewed monasteries and hospices for the poor and the elderly.

sections.h2: Boniface and the Rebuilding of Monte Cassino
paras: In 719 Gregory received the English monk Wynfrith in Rome, gave him the name Boniface, and commissioned him to preach to the pagan peoples east of the Rhine. In 722 he consecrated him a bishop, bound him by oath to the Roman see, and gave him letters of recommendation to Charles Martel. Boniface became the great apostle of Germany. Gregory also sent envoys to organize the church in Bavaria at the request of Duke Theodo.

Monte Cassino, the monastery of St. Benedict, had lain in ruins since the Lombards destroyed it in the late sixth century. Around 717, with Gregory's encouragement, the monk Petronax of Brescia led its refoundation, and it became once again a major center of Benedictine life. In 721 Gregory held a synod in Rome that issued canons on marriage, forbidding unions within close degrees of kinship and with consecrated women.

sections.h2: Leo III, Iconoclasm, and the Donation of Sutri
paras: In the 720s Emperor Leo III imposed heavy new taxes on Italy, which Gregory resisted, and imperial officials reportedly plotted against his life. When Leo moved against the veneration of icons around 726–730, Gregory opposed the policy firmly. Letters attributed to him defending icons survive, but their authenticity is debated. Even so, he discouraged Italian rebels from setting up a rival emperor, seeking to defend the faith without breaking with the empire.

The Lombard king Liutprand, meanwhile, was expanding his territory. In 728 he seized the fortress of Sutri north of Rome but, at Gregory's urging, gave it back as a gift to the apostles Peter and Paul. Historians often regard this Donation of Sutri as the first territorial grant that would grow into the Papal States. Gregory died on 11 February 731, his feast day.

keyFacts: Born in Rome; former librarian of the Roman Church
Commissioned St. Boniface (719) and consecrated him bishop (722)
Held the Synod of Rome (721) on marriage law
Received the Donation of Sutri from King Liutprand (728); feast day February 11

faqs.question: How was Pope Gregory II connected to St. Boniface?
faqs.answer: Gregory gave the English monk Wynfrith the name Boniface in 719, sent him to evangelize the Germanic peoples, and consecrated him a bishop in 722.

faqs.question: What was the Donation of Sutri?
faqs.answer: In 728 the Lombard king Liutprand returned the captured town of Sutri to the papacy as a gift to the apostles Peter and Paul. It is often considered the first step in the formation of the Papal States.

faqs.question: How did Gregory II respond to iconoclasm?
faqs.answer: He opposed Emperor Leo III's measures against the veneration of icons, while still urging Italians not to revolt against the empire or set up a rival emperor.
